packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-04 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING (almost nothing securely read)

Exposure statement
No proposed identification of work or author, and no earlier reading, reached me in my context. I opened only PROMPT.md and image-001..018.jpg (plus the filtered filename listing described in packet-01.txt). Nothing else beyond the rules.

Layout survey (observation)
- image-001: overview of one face (face 1) of a tall narrow paper leaf or strip, about 10.5 cm wide and 20 cm tall by the ruler, portrait, with a horizontal fold across the middle, wormholes, losses at the top and right edges, and brown paste/leather residue over much of the surface. It looks like binding waste.
- image-010: overview of the other face (face 2), the same outline mirrored; paler and even more abraded. Laid lines of the paper are visible as fine horizontal ribbing (image-013, -015), so the support is paper.
- Tiles, face 1 (2 wide by 4 high): image-002 top left, -003 top right, -004 upper-middle left, -005 upper-middle right, -006 lower-middle left, -007 lower-middle right, -008 bottom left, -009 bottom right. Neighbours overlap by two or three lines.
- Tiles, face 2 (2 wide by 4 high): image-011 top left, -012 top right, -013 upper-middle left, -014 upper-middle right, -015 lower-middle left, -016 lower-middle right, -017 bottom left, -018 bottom right.
- Script: a loose, fairly large cursive in a thin ink now washed to pale grey, with long descenders, doubled tall letters (ff / ss shapes), and frequent superscript abbreviation curls. Lines are irregular in length and spacing, and several begin with an enlarged or looped letter. No rubrication, no ruling, no running title, no gloss visible.
- Face 1: about 12 lines above the fold, starting at the top-left edge (first lines very short or lost under residue at the right); a blank band at the fold; then about 20 lines below it. Below the fold a second, narrower run of short lines stands at the right (image-005 foot, image-007), offset from the left-hand lines; whether this is a second column, a set of right-hand entries, or line ends of the same lines I cannot decide.
- Face 2: writing survives only as grey traces, mostly along the right side (image-012, -014, -016, -018); the left half looks blank or lost.
- Tentative interpretation: the irregular short lines, the repeated opening shapes, and the offset right-hand items make this look more like notes, a list or a draft than a formally laid-out book page. That is an impression from layout only.

Areas selected / unread
- I tried every tile. The only places where letter shapes separate from the stains are image-002/-004 (face 1, above the fold), image-006/-007 (face 1, just below the fold), and a few words in image-016 (face 2).
- Everything else is unread: face 1 bottom third (image-008, -009), face 1 right side above the fold (image-003, -005: residue only), and nearly all of face 2.
- I could not establish the language with confidence. Some groups look Latin with abbreviations (q with superscript, a "d(e)" at line openings); the recurring group I transcribe as "hoff" and some endings could equally be vernacular. I therefore give letter shapes, not words, and I have not expanded anything I could not see.

What I would actually rely on
- The physical description and layout above.
- The recurrence of one short group with a doubled tall letter ("hoff"/"hoſſ") three or four times in the upper block of face 1 (image-002 l.2, l.9, l.10; image-004 l.6), and of line openings in "q'" and "d(e)".
- No continuous phrase. Nothing here is good enough to test against a source.

Limitations
- The ink is washed almost to nothing and sits at about the same tone as the stains; where I give letters they are the darkest strokes only, and whole words may be misdivided.
- I cannot say which face is recto, whether the leaf is complete in width, or whether the right-hand items on face 1 form a column.
- The language is undetermined.
- Helpful next images: UV fluorescence and infrared of both faces; a raking-light image; and a strong contrast stretch of the blue channel for image-002, -004, -006, -007 and -016.
